## Item 1 — symlink safety in `clean_output_dir` [SECURITY]

**File:** `spec-core/src/generator.rs:103`  
**Priority:** High — latent footgun. Low probability in normal use; real risk if anyone
runs `spec generate` on a directory containing symlinks.

### Problem

`clean_output_dir` walks the target directories to delete `.rs` files using
`WalkDir::new(&target).follow_links(true)`. If a symlink exists inside the output tree
pointing outside it, the cleaner follows it and deletes `.rs` files in that external
location. The `starts_with(base)` guard runs on the *target directory* before the walk
starts — it does not check each individual file path during the walk.

```rust
// spec-core/src/generator.rs:103 — current (unsafe)
for entry in WalkDir::new(&target).follow_links(true) {
```

### Fix

Change `follow_links(true)` to `follow_links(false)` in `clean_output_dir` only.

```rust
// spec-core/src/generator.rs:103 — after fix
for entry in WalkDir::new(&target).follow_links(false) {
```

**Do NOT change** the `follow_links(true)` calls in `spec-core/src/loader.rs` (lines 83
and 112). Those are intentional: users should be able to symlink directories of spec
files into their units tree.

### Verification

The existing test `test_clean_output_dir_scoped_and_marker_safe` in
`spec-core/src/generator.rs` still passes after the change. Optionally add a test:
create a symlink inside the output tree pointing to a file outside it, run
`clean_output_dir`, and assert the external file was NOT deleted.

## Item 2 — cache compiled JSON schema [PERFORMANCE]

**File:** `spec-core/src/validator.rs:32–39`  
**Priority:** Medium — no correctness issue, but every `spec validate` on a directory
with N files compiles the schema N times. Adds ~10ms × N of unnecessary startup cost.

### Problem

`validate_json_value` deserializes and compiles the embedded JSON schema on every call:

```rust
// spec-core/src/validator.rs:32 — current (recompiles per call)
fn validate_json_value(spec_json: &Value, file_path: &str) -> Result<()> {
    let schema_json: Value = serde_json::from_str(SCHEMA_JSON)?;
    let schema = jsonschema::draft7::new(&schema_json).map_err(|e| { ... })?;
    ...
}
```

### Fix

Use `std::sync::OnceLock` to compile once and reuse. Add a new private function that
returns a reference to the cached validator, then call it from `validate_json_value`.

```rust
// spec-core/src/validator.rs — after fix

use std::sync::OnceLock;

static COMPILED_SCHEMA: OnceLock<jsonschema::Validator> = OnceLock::new();

fn compiled_schema() -> Result<&'static jsonschema::Validator> {
    COMPILED_SCHEMA.get_or_try_init(|| {
        let schema_json: Value = serde_json::from_str(SCHEMA_JSON)
            .map_err(SpecError::Json)?;
        jsonschema::draft7::new(&schema_json).map_err(|e| SpecError::SchemaValidation {
            message: format!("Schema compilation failed: {e}"),
            path: String::new(),
        })
    })
}

fn validate_json_value(spec_json: &Value, file_path: &str) -> Result<()> {
    let schema = compiled_schema()?;
    match schema.validate(spec_json) {
        Ok(()) => Ok(()),
        Err(error) => Err(SpecError::SchemaValidation {
            message: error.to_string(),
            path: file_path.to_string(),
        }),
    }
}
```

> **Note:** `OnceLock::get_or_try_init` is stable since Rust 1.70. The workspace MSRV is
> 1.89.0 so this is fine.

### Verification

All existing validator tests pass unchanged. The observable difference is faster
`spec validate` on directories with many files.

## Item 3 — release build matrix missing from CI [P1 RELEASE BLOCKER]

**File:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`  
**Priority:** P1 — explicitly called out as a release blocker in `TODOS.md`

### Problem

The current CI workflow only has a single `test` job running on `ubuntu-latest`. No
binary artifacts, no release job, no cross-platform matrix. `TODOS.md` requires:

- Build matrix: linux/darwin × amd64/arm64
- Trigger: tag push → GitHub Release with binaries + checksums

This blocks the M1 release.

### Fix

Add a second job to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that triggers on tag pushes and builds
cross-compiled binaries for all four targets. Recommended approach: use
[`cross`](https://github.com/cross-rs/cross) for Linux cross-compilation and
GitHub-hosted macOS runners for darwin targets.

Suggested matrix targets:

| OS | Arch | Target triple | Runner |
|----|------|---------------|--------|
| Linux | amd64 | `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` | `ubuntu-latest` via `cross` |
| Linux | arm64 | `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` | `ubuntu-latest` via `cross` |
| macOS | amd64 | `x86_64-apple-darwin` | `macos-latest` |
| macOS | arm64 | `aarch64-apple-darwin` | `macos-latest` (cross-compile) |

The release job should:
1. Build each target binary with `cross build --release --target <triple>`
2. Strip the binary
3. Upload all 4 binaries + SHA256 checksums as GitHub Release assets

Also see Item 4 (pin action SHAs) which should be done at the same time.

### Reference

`TODOS.md` entry: "Set up GitHub Actions for automated builds and releases" and
"Cross-compilation setup for CI — Build matrix (linux/darwin x amd64/arm64) requires
cross-compilation tooling... P1 — blocks release."

## Item 4 — pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs [SUPPLY CHAIN]

**File:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:13–20`  
**Priority:** Low-Medium — affects CI security, not the binary itself

### Problem

All three action references use mutable version tags that could be silently updated:

```yaml
uses: actions/checkout@v4            # mutable tag
uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable  # mutable tag  
uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2         # mutable tag
```

A tag can be force-pushed. If any of these repos is compromised, the next CI run picks
up the malicious version automatically.

### Fix

Pin each action to its commit SHA. Resolved SHAs as of 2026-04-01:

```yaml
uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683      # v4.2.2
uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@4f366e621dc797748a6153c4595cebf57c154ac  # stable 2025-01
uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@9bdad043e88c75890e36ad3bbc8d08f825e1f6cf   # v2.7.8
```

> **Note:** Verify these SHAs are still current before applying — check each repo's
> releases page. The SHA values above are illustrative; use the actual latest stable
> release SHAs.

Keep the human-readable version tag as a comment:

```yaml
uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683  # v4.2.2
```

## Item 5 — unused public API in `spec-core/src/loader.rs` [API HYGIENE]

**File:** `spec-core/src/loader.rs`  
**Priority:** Low — must fix before first `crates.io` publish

### Problem

Four public functions have zero callers outside their own test blocks. They are early
design artefacts — the CLI uses its own `WalkDir` loop in `commands.rs` and never calls
these. Once `spec-core` is published, they become locked public API:

| Function | Line | Status |
|----------|------|--------|
| `load_directory_collect_all` | 108 | No callers outside tests |
| `output_dir_for_spec` | 151 | No callers outside tests |
| `output_file_path` | 163 | No callers outside tests |
| `mod_rs_dir` | 185 | No callers outside tests |

`load_directory` (line 79) is also uncalled from the CLI but is a legitimate public API
for library consumers — keep it `pub`.

### Fix

Change the four functions above from `pub` to `pub(crate)`:

```rust
// loader.rs — change these four signatures
pub(crate) fn load_directory_collect_all<P: AsRef<Path>>(dir: P) -> DirectoryLoadReport
pub(crate) fn output_dir_for_spec(output_base: impl AsRef<Path>, module_path: &str) -> PathBuf
pub(crate) fn output_file_path(output_base: impl AsRef<Path>, id: &str) -> PathBuf
pub(crate) fn mod_rs_dir(output_base: impl AsRef<Path>, module_path: &str) -> PathBuf
```

Their existing tests are inside the same crate so `pub(crate)` is sufficient.

If any of these are intentionally part of the public library API (e.g. for future
programmatic use by spec-aware tools), leave them `pub` and add a `#[doc]` comment
explaining their intended use. The decision should be deliberate before publish.

## Item 6 — remove unreachable `From<jsonschema::ValidationError>` impl [DEAD CODE]

**File:** `spec-core/src/lib.rs:66–73`  
**Priority:** Low

### Problem

```rust
impl From<jsonschema::ValidationError<'_>> for SpecError {
    fn from(err: jsonschema::ValidationError) -> Self {
        SpecError::SemanticValidation {
            message: err.to_string(),
            path: String::new(), // This should be set by the caller
        }
    }
}
```

This `From` impl is never invoked. All jsonschema validation errors in `validator.rs`
are converted manually (so the file path can be populated). The comment "This should be
set by the caller" describes an impossible guarantee — `From` gives no mechanism to
inject context after the conversion.

If this impl is used via the `?` operator anywhere, the resulting `SpecError` will have
`path: ""`, making the error message useless for debugging.

### Fix

Remove the impl entirely:

```rust
// Delete lines 66–73 of spec-core/src/lib.rs
impl From<jsonschema::ValidationError<'_>> for SpecError { ... }
```

Verify with `cargo check` that nothing breaks — if it does, the call site should be
converting manually with the file path populated.
